lessons.title: Read bubbles and printed effects
lessons.description: Distinguish a character’s line from sound, movement or feeling described on an original comic page.
lessons.canDo: Identify what is spoken and keep an uncertain interpretation open

lessons.title: Recover a casual line from its context
lessons.description: Read omitted particles, expressive kana and reactions in four original panels.
lessons.canDo: Recover a familiar object particle and read effects without inventing an event

grammar.title: Separate a line from a printed effect
grammar.formation: A speech bubble gives an attributed utterance. Printed 擬音語/擬態語 may describe sound, motion, silence or feeling; read the surrounding panel.
grammar.explanation: This is a reading convention, not a new inflection. A printed effect need not be something a character said. A mimetic word can describe a state with no audible sound. One form can have several meanings, so use the depicted situation and nearby words. Retrieve earlier 台詞, 人物 and 場面.
grammar.example: 吹き出しの台詞を読む。
grammar.translation: Read the line in the speech bubble.

examples.ja: {吹|ふ}き{出|だ}しの{台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}む。
examples.en: Read the line in the speech bubble.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}の{背景|はいけい}に「ざあざあ」と{書|か}いてある。
examples.en: The rainy background has the printed effect zāzā.

examples.ja: 「しーん」は{人物|じんぶつ}の{声|こえ}とは{限|かぎ}らない。
examples.en: Shīn is not necessarily a character’s spoken voice.

grammar.mistake: Do not assign every printed effect to a speaker or force every use of one word into a single category.

grammar.title: Read the word with the action it modifies
grammar.formation: Taught combinations: じっと + 見る; にっこり + 笑う; どきどき + する. Some mimetics take と before a verb. Learn the actual combination.
grammar.explanation: Adverbial words describe how an action happens; some also combine with する to name a state. と is common with certain sound or manner expressions, but neither adding と nor adding する works identically for every word. These models teach combinations, not a universal suffix rule. ごろごろ in a sentence about staying home differs from rumbling thunder.
grammar.example: 視線を変えずに、枠をじっと見る。
grammar.translation: Look intently at the frame without changing the direction of your gaze.

examples.ja: {視線|しせん}を{変|か}えずに、{枠|わく}をじっと{見|み}る。
examples.en: Look intently at the frame without changing the direction of your gaze.

examples.ja: ユイがにっこり{笑|わら}った。
{雨|あめ}の{音|おと}を{聞|き}いて、どきどきした。
examples.en: Hearing the rain, I felt my heart pounding.

grammar.mistake: Do not assume every word ending in り takes する, or every mimetic word represents an audible noise.

grammar.title: Recover the role of an omitted particle
grammar.formation: In familiar casual context, object を or topic は may be omitted: 傘を見た？→傘見た？ Keep the role recoverable; restore particles in explicit form practice.
grammar.explanation: Short casual manga lines may leave out a particle that context supplies. 傘見た？ asks whether someone saw the umbrella; it doesn’t make 傘 the person doing the seeing. Retain particles that distinguish who did what, contrast or a needed relationship. This is recognition, not an instruction to remove all particles or use a casual fragment in a teacher email.
grammar.translation: Did you read this panel? (casual object particle omitted)

examples.en: Did you read this panel? (casual object particle omitted)
Did you see the umbrella? (casual object particle omitted)

examples.ja: {台本|だいほん}は{読|よ}んだけど、{続|つづ}きはまだ。
examples.en: I read the script, but not the rest yet; the contrasting は is retained.

grammar.mistake: A missing を in clear casual context is not automatically an error. Do not delete と/で/の blindly or invert the actor and object.

grammar.title: Recognise an abrupt ending and a long vowel
grammar.formation: Between consonants, small っ marks a consonant closure. At the end of あっ！ it marks an abrupt cutoff, not a separately spoken つ. ー/〜 may stretch the preceding vowel in expressive writing.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve ordinary small-っ and long-vowel reading. Printed reactions can exaggerate length; they are not models for prolonging every lesson vowel. あっ is a brief reaction, while あー can be drawn out. A longer reaction doesn’t by itself prove anger or happiness; context matters. Read しーん with a long vowel, not as しん.

examples.ja: 「あっ！」と{短|みじか}く{声|こえ}を{出|だ}した。
「あー、{分|わ}かった」と{言|い}った。
examples.en: They said a drawn-out Ah, I understand.

examples.ja: {部屋|へや}はしーんとしていた。

grammar.mistake: Do not pronounce terminal っ as tsu or treat expressive length as the correct length of a single kana drill.

grammar.title: A reaction or a question is not proof of an event
grammar.formation: Question intonation/？ asks; an exclamation reacts. Read the reply and later panel before treating a guess as a fact.
grammar.explanation: Reuse earlier の？, かな and っけ. A speaker who asks 雷？ has not established that thunder occurred; ごろごろ can also describe another action. A relieved ほっとした needs an event to interpret it. Printed sweat or tears alone doesn’t identify the cause. These are discourse cues rather than a certified JLPT grammar list.
grammar.example: 「雷？」と聞いたが、返事はまだだった。
grammar.translation: They asked Thunder?, but there was no reply yet.

examples.ja: 「{雷|かみなり}？」と{聞|き}いたが、{返事|へんじ}はまだだった。
examples.en: They asked Thunder?, but there was no reply yet.

examples.ja: {傘|かさ}が{見|み}つかって、ほっとした。
examples.en: They felt relieved when the umbrella was found.

examples.ja: どきどきしている{理由|りゆう}は、{次|つぎ}のコマで{分|わ}かった。
examples.en: The next panel revealed why their heart was pounding.

grammar.mistake: A question mark is not a factual confirmation. Do not assign a cause to an emotion from one effect alone.

dialogues.title: A comic page beside the script
dialogues.scene: At the café, Misaki shows Bao an original comic page after the headphone review. They distinguish bubbles and printed effects. They have only read the first two panels; neither knows who is outside the door.

lines.speaker: Misaki

lines.romaji: Tsugi wa kono manga, yonde minai? E ga kirei nan da yo.
lines.meaning: Want to read this comic next? The drawings are beautiful.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {吹|ふ}き{出|だ}しの{中|なか}は{人物|じんぶつ}の{台詞|せりふ}だね。でも、{枠|わく}の{外|そと}にある{文字|もじ}は、{全部|ぜんぶ}{声|こえ}に{出|だ}したのかな。
lines.romaji: Fukidashi no naka wa jinbutsu no serifu da ne. Demo, waku no soto ni aru moji wa, zenbu koe ni dashita no kana.
lines.meaning: The bubbles contain the characters’ lines. But did someone say all the words outside the frames aloud?

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: そうとは{限|かぎ}らないよ。{効果音|こうかおん}の{文字|もじ}もある。{雨|あめ}の{背景|はいけい}にある{擬音語|ぎおんご}は、{音|おと}の{描写|びょうしゃ}だね。
lines.romaji: Sō to wa kagiranai yo. Kōkaon no moji mo aru. Ame no haikei ni aru giongo wa, oto no byōsha da ne.
lines.meaning: Not necessarily. There are written sound effects too. A sound word in a rainy background depicts sound.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: そうか。{音|おと}がなくても、どんな{気持|きも}ちか{分|わ}かるんだね。
lines.romaji: Sō ka. Oto ga nakute mo, donna kimochi ka wakaru n da ne.
lines.meaning: I see. Even without a sound, you can tell how someone feels.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {最初|さいしょ}の{場面|ばめん}では、ドアの{向|む}こうで{物音|ものおと}がする。{人物|じんぶつ}の{視線|しせん}も、そこに{向|む}いているね。
lines.romaji: Saisho no bamen de wa, doa no mukō de monooto ga suru. Jinbutsu no shisen mo, soko ni muite iru ne.
lines.meaning: In the first scene, there is a noise on the other side of the door. The character’s gaze is directed there too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {足音|あしおと}みたいだけど、{誰|だれ}かはまだ{分|わ}からない。{語尾|ごび}や{台詞|せりふ}を{聞|き}けば、{後|あと}で{分|わ}かるかも。
lines.romaji: Ashioto mitai da kedo, dare ka wa mada wakaranai. Gobi ya serifu o kikeba, ato de wakaru kamo.
lines.meaning: It seems like footsteps, but I don’t know who it’s yet. The ending or line may tell us later.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {次|つぎ}のコマには{余白|よはく}が{多|おお}いね。{誰|だれ}も{話|はな}さない{沈黙|ちんもく}や{静寂|せいじゃく}を{表|あらわ}しているのかも。
lines.romaji: Tsugi no koma ni wa yohaku ga ōi ne. Dare mo hanasanai chinmoku ya seijaku o arawashite iru no kamo.
lines.meaning: The next panel has a lot of blank space. It may convey silence or stillness while no one speaks.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {汗|あせ}も{涙|なみだ}も{描|えが}いてあるね。{怖|こわ}かったのかな、それとも{嬉|うれ}しかったのかな。{続|つづ}きを{読|よ}もう。
lines.romaji: Ase mo namida mo egaite aru ne. Kowakatta no kana, sore tomo ureshikatta no kana. Tsuzuki o yomō.
lines.meaning: There’s sweat and tears in the drawing. Was she scared, or happy? Let’s read on.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: うん。{吹|ふ}き{出|だ}しの{台詞|せりふ}も{気|き}になるね。
lines.romaji: Un. Fukidashi no serifu mo ki ni naru ne.
lines.meaning: Yeah. I’m curious about what’s in the speech bubble too.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: まだ{二|ふた}つのコマだけだもんね。ドアの{外|そと}は{誰|だれ}だろう。{早|はや}く{次|つぎ}が{見|み}たいな。
lines.romaji: Mada futatsu no koma dake da mon ne. Doa no soto wa dare darō. Hayaku tsugi ga mitai na.
lines.meaning: We’ve only seen two panels. Who’s outside the door? I can’t wait to see the next one.

dialogues.title: A missing particle, and the panel after it
dialogues.scene: Bao and Misaki read the remaining original panels. In the comic, Yui asks Ren about her umbrella. Kenta arrives later, wet from the rain; he is unharmed and had stopped to buy bread. They discuss meanings in context, without inventing a thunderstorm.

lines.romaji: Kono hon, parapara mekuru dake de mo wakuwaku suru ne. Saisho no koma, jitto mite miyō.
lines.meaning: Even leafing through this book is exciting. Let’s look closely at the first panel.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ユイの{台詞|せりふ}は「{傘|かさ}{見|み}た？」だね。きょろきょろ{探|さが}している。この{場面|ばめん}なら、{傘|かさ}を{見|み}たか{聞|き}いているんだ。
lines.romaji: Yui no serifu wa kasa mita da ne. Kyorokyoro sagashite iru. Kono bamen nara, kasa o mita ka kiite irun da.
lines.meaning: Yui’s line is Did you see the umbrella? She is looking around for it. In this scene she asks whether someone saw it.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {次|つぎ}のコマでレンが{棚|たな}を{指|さ}して、ユイはにっこり{笑|わら}った。ほっとしたのは、{自分|じぶん}の{傘|かさ}が{見|み}つかったからだね。
lines.romaji: Tsugi no koma de Ren ga tana o sashite, Yui wa nikkori waratta. Hotto shita no wa, jibun no kasa ga mitsukatta kara da ne.
lines.meaning: In the next panel Ren points to a shelf and Yui smiles. She is relieved because her umbrella was found.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {外|そと}では{雨|あめ}がぽつぽつ{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}めて、その{後|あと}ざあざあ{降|ふ}っている。ごろごろという{文字|もじ}は、この{場面|ばめん}にはないね。
lines.romaji: Soto de wa ame ga potsupotsu furihajimete, sono ato zāzā futte iru. Gorogoro to iu moji wa, kono bamen ni wa nai ne.
lines.meaning: Outside, rain starts with a few drops and then falls heavily. The word gorogoro is not printed in this scene.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: ごろごろって、{雷|かみなり}にも{使|つか}うよね。でも「{家|いえ}でごろごろする」は、のんびりしてるってことか。
lines.romaji: Gorogoro tte, kaminari ni mo tsukau yo ne. Demo ie de gorogoro suru wa, nonbiri shiteru tte koto ka.
lines.meaning: Gorogoro is used for thunder too, right? But gorogoro at home means lounging around.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ドアががたがたと{鳴|な}って、{足音|あしおと}がぴたりと{止|と}まった。{人物|じんぶつ}が{誰|だれ}か、はらはらしながら{読|よ}んだよ。
lines.romaji: Doa ga gatagata to natte, ashioto ga pitari to tomatta. Jinbutsu ga dare ka, harahara shinagara yonda yo.
lines.meaning: The door rattles and the footsteps stop abruptly. I read anxiously, wondering who the character was.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: {最後|さいご}にケンタが{来|き}たね。ばたばた{走|はし}っていたけど、パンを{買|か}っていて{遅|おそ}くなっただけだよ。{事故|じこ}ではなかった。
lines.romaji: Saigo ni Kenta ga kita ne. Batabata hashitte ita kedo, pan o katte ite osoku natta dake da yo. Jiko de wa nakatta.
lines.meaning: Kenta arrives at the end. He was hurrying, but was only late because he had stopped to buy bread. It was not an accident.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: 「あっ！」って{短|みじか}く{言|い}ってるね。びっくりした{感|かん}じがする。
lines.romaji: At! Tte mijikaku itteru ne. Bikkuri shita kanji ga suru.
lines.meaning: That’s a short “Ah!” It sounds like surprise.

lines.speaker: Misaki
lines.line: 「しーん」で、{急|きゅう}に{静|しず}かになったね。さっきまで{足音|あしおと}がしてたのに。
lines.romaji: Shīn de, kyū ni shizuka ni natta ne. Sakki made ashioto ga shiteta no ni.
lines.meaning: Shīn makes it suddenly silent. There were footsteps just a moment ago.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ケンタは{昨夜|さくや}ぐっすり{寝|ね}たんだね。{僕|ぼく}だけどきどきしちゃったよ。{次|つぎ}の{話|はなし}も{読|よ}みたいな。
lines.romaji: Kenta wa sakuya gussuri neta n da ne. Boku dake dokidoki shichatta yo. Tsugi no hanashi mo yomitai na.
lines.meaning: So Kenta slept soundly last night. I was the one with my heart racing! I want to read the next story too.

exercises.prompt: What must be separated from a character’s spoken line?
options: Printed effects that can depict sound or a state
Every word in a speech bubble
The measured weight of the headphones
exercises.explain: They distinguish the bubble’s 台詞 from printed effects; not all printed text was said aloud.

exercises.prompt: What do Bao and Misaki still not know after two panels?
options: Whether the frame contains any lettering
Whether the page is a product specification
exercises.explain: The last line explicitly leaves the person outside unidentified.

exercises.prompt: Why should they read on before interpreting drawn sweat or tears?
options: Several causes are possible; the nearby scene matters
Every written effect is an actor’s voice
exercises.explain: They reject a single automatic cause and check the context.

exercises.context: Notation practice: choose the written short reaction Ah!, ending abruptly without an extra spoken tsu.
exercises.line: {人物|じんぶつ}の{短|みじか}い{台詞|せりふ}は「＿＿！」だった。
exercises.explain: The terminal small っ marks a cutoff; it’s not the full-size つ sound.

exercises.context: Notation practice: choose a drawn-out Aa with the long-vowel bar ー.
exercises.line: {人物|じんぶつ}は「＿＿、{分|わ}かった」と{言|い}った。
exercises.explain: The bar stretches the preceding vowel; the requested printed form is long, not an abrupt cutoff.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki; keep the distinction between printed effect and utterance.
exercises.line: {効果音|こうかおん}の{文字|もじ}も、{全部|ぜんぶ}{人物|じんぶつ}が{言|い}ったの？
options: そうとは{限|かぎ}らないね。{台詞|せりふ}と、{場面|ばめん}の{合図|あいず}を{分|わ}けて{読|よ}もう。
うん。{全部|ぜんぶ}の{文字|もじ}を{同|おな}じ{人|ひと}が{言|い}ったよ。
{文字|もじ}はないから、{台詞|せりふ}も{読|よ}めないよ。
exercises.explain: The first keeps printed effects distinct; the others invent a universal utterance or deny the printed page.

exercises.meaning: Before interpreting the depiction of tears, read the next panel.
tiles: {涙|なみだ}の{描写|びょうしゃ}を
{解釈|かいしゃく}する{前|まえ}に、
exercises.explain: The temporal order is read context before deciding the cause.

exercises.prompt: What does Yui’s 傘見た？ ask in this scene?
exercises.explain: The object を is omitted in casual context; the next panel answers where her umbrella is.

exercises.prompt: Why does Yui smile and feel relieved?
options: Thunder was confirmed by the headphones
exercises.explain: Ren points to the shelf and Yui recognises her umbrella.

exercises.prompt: What explanation does the final panel give for Kenta’s lateness?
options: He was injured in an accident
He was testing the noise-reduction function
exercises.explain: Misaki gives the reason and says it was not an accident.

exercises.context: Explicit form practice: restore the omitted object を in the casual line 傘見た？.
exercises.explain: The umbrella is the thing seen, not the place or recipient. The casual version without を was understandable.

exercises.context: Combination practice: report a pounding heart with the taught どきどきする, in the past.
exercises.line: {台詞|せりふ}を{読|よ}んで、どきどき＿＿。
exercises.explain: どきどきした reports the state; no noun-particle を is inserted into this combination.

exercises.context: Reply casually. Interpret ごろごろ from the sentence 家でごろごろする, without inventing weather.
exercises.line: ごろごろって、{必|かなら}ず{雷|かみなり}の{音|おと}なの？
options: この{場面|ばめん}では、{家|いえ}で{何|なに}もしないで{過|す}ごす{意味|いみ}だね。{解釈|かいしゃく}には{前後|ぜんご}が{必要|ひつよう}だよ。
うん。どの{場面|ばめん}でも{雷|かみなり}だけだよ。
ごろごろは、{全|すべ}ての{製品|せいひん}の{仕様|しよう}だよ。
exercises.explain: The home-resting sentence supports lounging, not thunder. The same form has several uses.

exercises.meaning: I read the line as a cue, found the umbrella, and felt relieved.
tiles: {台詞|せりふ}を{合図|あいず}にして、
exercises.explain: The found object supplies a reason for relief; the reaction is not free-standing proof of another event.

exercises.prompt: Whose umbrella is identified in panel 2?
exercises.explain: Yui says 私のだ after the blue umbrella is identified.

exercises.prompt: What is しーん in panel 3?
options: A printed depiction of a silent pause
exercises.explain: It’s marked as an effect and nobody speaks in that panel.

exercises.prompt: Why is Kenta late, according to his line?
exercises.explain: He says パンを買ってた; being wet is separate and he denies injury.

exercises.prompt: What does ごろごろ refer to in Kenta’s last line?
exercises.explain: 家で gives the home-resting context; nothing confirms thunder.

grammar: terminal small っ and vowel length
watch.prompt: Optionally examine a panel or subtitle from your own media. Recover an omitted role from context; distinguish a guess, spoken line and printed effect.

recycling.reason: Friends respond to a comic and a cliffhanger; unrelated product specifications and interpretation disclaimers were removed.
